evidence: Receiving online DO2 sensor: 10.21 mg/L at t=239.0 h, then 1.92 mg/L at t=240.0 h — abrupt collapse
Receiving online DO2 sensor, t=240–259 h: all 20 readings below the 2.0 mg/L hard limit; last value 1.46 mg/L at t=259 h; mean of last 10 = 1.61 mg/L; linear drift -0.022 mg/L/h
Receiving delayed product assays: P = 0.02 g/L @119 h, 0.95 g/L @179 h, 2.62 g/L @239 h — metabolically active batch, not product-limited
allowed_actions: combined = [0.8, 1.15]; minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0
submission.rationale: Receiving DO collapsed from ~10.2 mg/L (t=239 h) to ~1.9 mg/L (t=240 h) and has remained below the 2.0 mg/L hard limit for 20 consecutive online sensor readings, currently ~1.46–1.6 mg/L and still drifting down. KEEP is predicted to keep violating the hard constraint and is rejected. Product assays (0.02 → 0.95 → 2.62 g/L) show a viable, producing culture, so stop (zero production) is unnecessary if a bounded feasible plan exists. The deficit (~0.4 mg/L and growing) and the abrupt step-like collapse (consistent with an air-side delivery loss coinciding with rising OUR) justify acting on both oxygen supply and demand: combined (feed ×0.8, air ×1.15) reduces OUR 20% while boosting aeration 15%, the least-product-loss plan with evidence supporting restoration of DO ≥ 2 mg/L. increase_air alone leaves OUR growth unchecked; reduce_feed alone leaves the apparent aeration deficit unaddressed; strong_feed_reduction (×0.6) sacrifices more product mass than evidence requires. No extra assay requested: DO is a real-time online measurement and a 4 h assay turnaround would delay intervention in an active constraint violation.
submission.uncertainty: No calibrated physics model was run; the ~0.4 mg/L deficit and -0.02 mg/L/h drift come from raw sensor data with visible noise (~±0.2 mg/L). The effectiveness of ×1.15 aeration against the apparent delivery fault is unverified — if the step change reflects a mechanical air failure uncaptured by the multiplier, combined could still be insufficient and a stronger action or stop could become necessary at review. Hidden receiving-process parameters and the future OUR trajectory are unknown. Sensitivity-style reasoning above is qualitative, not probabilistic.

evidence: Receiving online DO2 sensor: values 1.35-2.22 mg/L from t=48.0h to t=51.8h, below the 2 mg/L hard limit for ~4 h
Forward model strong_feed_reduction: post-decision below_limit 9.2 h, min DO 0.96 mg/L, 0/5 sensitivity members feasible
Forward model combined: post-decision below_limit 11.4 h, min DO 0.84 mg/L, 0/5 feasible
Forward model keep: post-decision below_limit 8.2 h, min DO 0.90 mg/L, 0/5 feasible
Forward model increase_air and reduce_feed: also infeasible (min DO 0.77 / 0.74 mg/L)
Latest product assay available at 51.8h: 2.62 g/L at t=47.8h
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 has been below the 2 mg/L hard limit since ~48 h (sensor reads 1.3-1.9 mg/L at 48-51.8 h and declining). The source-calibrated forward model predicts every remaining operating plan (keep, reduce_feed, increase_air, combined, strong_feed_reduction) violates the limit for the remaining run: centrally predicted post-decision minimum DO of 0.74-0.96 mg/L with 0 of 5 sensitivity members feasible in each case. Strong_feed_reduction (0.6x feed, 1.15x air) — the most aggressive intervention — still shows 9.2 h below the limit and min DO 0.96 mg/L. Per the decision priorities, a centrally predicted infeasible plan is not justified by any favorable sensitivity member, and no operating plan can be supported as meeting the constraint. Stop is therefore the only defensible decision, accepting zero counted production rather than violating the hard oxygen constraint.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is nominal, source-calibrated, and may mismatch the true receiving process (estimated transfer multiplier 0.41); actual DO recovery under strong_feed_reduction could differ. The DO sensor itself could be faulty, but the persistent multi-hour decline from ~10 to ~1.5 mg/L is consistent across many readings and corroborated by the model's estimated oxygen-transfer collapse at t=48 h. Even allowing substantial model error, the observed current DO (1.35-1.9 mg/L) is already below the limit and trending down, so no operating plan is plausibly feasible. If an intervention were needed, strong_feed_reduction would have the best predicted margin among actions, but its central prediction and full sensitivity set remain infeasible.
